name: Thunderbolt of Zeus
appearance: A bolt of lightning, hurled from the sky.
limitations: The weapon of the sky; not a common weapon, and bound to Zeus's will.
creation_story: Forged for Zeus by the Cyclopes after the Titanomachy. [S1]
origin_story: A product of the highest divine craft, the emblem of the new order. [S1]
confidence_note: Attested across Hesiod, Homer and the visual record; the Cyclopean forging is in the Theogony.
tier_rationale: DIVINE: the supreme weapon of the chief god, the instrument that overthrew the Titans and the emblem of cosmic order; not primordial (it is made, not self-existent).

power_profile.explanation: The thunderbolt is the supreme weapon of the sky; it is the instrument that overthrew the Titans and the Typhons.
The bolt is the emblem of Zeus' sovereignty over the cosmos and the order of the gods.
A projectile of the sky, striking from a distance across the world.
A product of divine (Cyclopean) craft; it is an instrument of the highest power.
It is the arbiter of Zeus's will, directed at hubris and disorder.

abilities.name: SKY-THUNDER
abilities.description: The thunderbolt is the weapon of the sky, the emblem of Zeus' sovereignty.

abilities.name: TITAN-SLAYER
abilities.description: It is the instrument by which Zeus overthrew the Titans.

abilities.name: HUBRIS-ARBITER
abilities.description: It is directed at hubris and disorder; it is the justice of the sky.

artwork.title: Zeus Casting Thunderbolts (Dodona, c. 470 BC)
artwork.depicts: No thunderbolt survives as an object. This is a 5th-century BCE sculpture of Zeus hurling his thunderbolt — an ancient depiction of the myth, not the object itself.

description_short: The thunderbolt of Zeus, the supreme weapon of the sky and the arbiter of order.
description_long: The thunderbolt (Bóltēs) is the supreme weapon of Zeus. In Hesiod's Theogony it is the instrument by which Zeus overthrew the Titans, forged for him by the Cyclopes. [S1] In the Iliad it is the emblem of Zeus' sovereignty, hurled at hubris and at the armies of disorder. [S2] It is the arbiter of the sky's justice.
interesting_facts: The thunderbolt is the Greek equivalent of the eschatological / sovereign sky-weapon.
uncertainty_notes: The "Cyclopean forging" is Hesiod's account; other traditions localize the craft differently.

name: Aegis
material: Goat-skin (per the name) set with metal and the Gorgoneion
appearance: A shield / breastplate, set with the Gorgoneion, surrounded by snakes or clouds in later art.
limitations: The emblem of Athena; not a common shield, and bound to the goddess.
creation_story: In some accounts given or made by Hephaestus; in others it is her own.
origin_story: The emblem of Athena's sovereignty over war and wisdom. [S1]
confidence_note: Attested across Homer, Hesiod and the visual record; the Gorgoneion detail is in the Theogony and the Iliad.
tier_rationale: DIVINE: the emblem of a chief goddess' sovereignty and terror, set with the Gorgoneion; a permanent, unbroken divine attribute.

power_profile.explanation: The Aegis is the shield/breastplate of Athena, the emblem of her unassailable protection.
It is the emblem of inviolability; it turns fear against the enemy.
The Gorgoneion (Medusa's head) is set in it; it is an instrument of divine terror.
It is the mark of Athena's sovereignty over war and wisdom.
No source describes the Aegis being broken; it is a permanent emblem of the goddess.

abilities.name: GORGOINE TERROR
abilities.description: The Gorgoneion (Medusa's head) set in the Aegis turns fear against the enemy.

abilities.name: INVIOLABLE SHIELD
abilities.description: The Aegis is the emblem of Athena's unassailable protection.

abilities.name: WEATHER-FRAME
abilities.description: Clouds and thunder surround the Aegis in some accounts; it is a frame of the storm.

artwork.title: Athena with the Kreuzbandaegis (ancient relief)
artwork.depicts: No Aegis survives as an object. This is an ancient relief of Athena wearing the aegis — an ancient depiction of the emblem, not the object itself.

description_short: The shield / breastplate of Athena, set with the Gorgoneion, the emblem of her terror and protection.
description_long: The Aegis ('the goat-skin') is the shield or breastplate of Athena. In Homer and Hesiod it is set with the Gorgoneion — the head of Medusa — and it is the emblem of her unassailable protection and of the terror she turns against her enemies. [S1][S2] In later accounts clouds and thunder surround it. It is the mark of Athena's sovereignty over war and wisdom.
interesting_facts: The Aegis is the Greek equivalent of the protective divine shield; the Gorgoneion is its terror.
uncertainty_notes: Whether the Aegis is a shield, a breastplate, or a cloak is debated; the sources use the word loosely.

name: Helmet of Hades
creator_name: The Cyclopes (in Hesiod) / Hephaestus (in some accounts)
appearance: A helm / cap; in later art a winged or darkened helmet.
limitations: The emblem of the underworld; not a common helm, and bound to the passage of the dead.
creation_story: In the Theogony, given by the Cyclopes to Zeus, who in turn gives it to Perseus. [S1]
origin_story: A product of the underworld's power, made wearable. [S1]
confidence_note: Attested in the Odyssey (Perseus) and the Theogony (given by the Cyclopes); the "invisibility" is the consistent property.
tier_rationale: LEGENDARY: a named divine instrument with a distinctive, repeated property (invisibility), central to a major myth (Perseus), but narrower in cosmological scope than the divine-tier emblem.

power_profile.explanation: Invisibility is a stealth and utility power (transformation into the unseen), not raw offensive might; scored so that a legendary helmet does not outrank divine-tier weapons in the card's interpretive PWR.
It grants stealth and passage; the wearer moves unseen.
A product of divine (Cyclopean / Hephaestean) craft; invisibility is a property of the underworld.
It is a tool of stealth and of the passage of the dead.

abilities.name: INVISIBILITY
abilities.description: It renders the wearer invisible; the power of the underworld made wearable.

abilities.name: PASSAGE OF THE DEAD
abilities.description: It is the emblem of the underworld and of the passage of the dead.

artwork.title: Corinthian Helmet (ancient)
artwork.depicts: No Helmet of Hades survives. This is a genuine ancient Corinthian helmet — a type-proxy showing the real object-class of the helm, not the mythic object of invisibility itself.

description_short: The helmet of Hades, which renders its wearer invisible — the power of the underworld made wearable.
description_long: The Helmet of Hades (also called the Helm of Darkness or the Cap of Invisibility) is the emblem of the underworld. In Homer it renders the wearer invisible; it is given to Perseus to slay Medusa and is associated with the passage of the dead. [S3] It is a product of divine craft, the power of the underworld made wearable.
interesting_facts: The Helm is the Greek equivalent of the "invisibility cloak" — a property of the underworld.
uncertainty_notes: Whether it is a helm or a cap is debated; the sources use different words. Its maker (Cyclopes vs. Hephaestus) varies by tradition.

name: Trident of Poseidon
limitations: The weapon of the sea; not a common weapon, and bound to Poseidon's will.
creation_story: Forged for Poseidon by the Cyclopes. [S1]
origin_story: A product of the highest divine craft, the emblem of the sea's order. [S1]
confidence_note: Attested across Homer, Hesiod and the visual record; the Cyclopean forging is in the Theogony.
tier_rationale: DIVINE: the emblem of a chief god's sovereignty over a whole realm (the sea and the earth), the instrument of earthquakes; not primordial (it is made, not self-existent).

power_profile.explanation: The trident strikes the sea and the land; it is the instrument of earthquakes and of the sea's power.
It is the emblem of Poseidon's sovereignty over the sea and the earth.
It stirs the sea, raises mountains, and splits the rock; it is the arbiter of the waters.
A spear-like weapon of the sea, striking from a distance.
A product of divine (Cyclopean) craft; it is an instrument of the sea's power.

abilities.name: SEA-STIR
abilities.description: It stirs the sea and raises the waves; the power of the waters made a weapon.

abilities.name: EARTHQUAKE
abilities.description: It strikes the land and raises mountains; the instrument of earthquakes.

abilities.name: SOVEREIGN OF THE SEA
abilities.description: It is the emblem of Poseidon's sovereignty over the sea and the earth.

artwork.title: Poseidon with Trident and Dolphin (ancient pinax)
artwork.depicts: No trident survives as an object. This is an ancient terracotta pinax of Poseidon holding his trident — an ancient depiction of the emblem, not the object itself.

description_short: The trident of Poseidon, the emblem of the sea and the earth, the instrument of earthquakes.
description_long: The trident is the weapon of Poseidon, the god of the sea. In Homer and Hesiod it is the emblem of his sovereignty over the waters and the earth; it stirs the sea, raises the waves, and strikes the land to raise mountains and cause earthquakes. [S1][S2] It is a product of divine (Cyclopean) craft. It is the arbiter of the waters and the emblem of the sea's power.
interesting_facts: The trident is the Greek equivalent of the sovereign sea-weapon; it is the emblem of earthquakes.
uncertainty_notes: The "Cyclopean forging" is Hesiod's account; the trident's exact make is not specified elsewhere.

name: Caduceus of Hermes
alternative_names: The Staff of the Two Serpents
material: Wood or metal set with two entwined serpents
appearance: A staff with two entwined serpents and (in later art) wings.
limitations: The emblem of the messenger; not a weapon, and bound to Hermes's passage.
creation_story: Its making is not specified in the surviving sources.
origin_story: The emblem of the messenger and the mediator, tied to the passage between worlds. [S3]
confidence_note: Attested in Homer as Hermes' staff; the "sleep/wake" property is in the Odyssey and later tradition; the medical use is a much later, separate association.
tier_rationale: LEGENDARY: a named divine instrument of a major god with a distinctive property (mediation / the passage between worlds), but narrower in cosmological scope than the divine-tier emblems.

power_profile.explanation: It is the instrument of the messenger and the mediator; it guides and reconciles.
In some accounts it can put the dead to sleep or wake them; it is an instrument of the passage between worlds.
It is the emblem of the messenger's passage; Hermes moves the world with it.
A tool of the messenger, the trader, and the guide of souls.

abilities.name: MEDIATOR
abilities.description: It is the instrument of the messenger and the mediator; it guides and reconciles.

abilities.name: SLEEP AND WAKING
abilities.description: In some accounts it can put the dead to sleep or wake them; the passage between worlds.

artwork.title: A Caduceus (Wellcome historical illustration)
artwork.depicts: No caduceus survives as a mythic object. This is a historical illustration of the caduceus (the staff of the two serpents) — a later depiction of the emblem, not an ancient object.

description_short: The caduceus of Hermes, the staff of the two serpents, the emblem of the messenger and the mediator.
description_long: The caduceus is the staff of Hermes, the messenger of the gods. In Homer it is the emblem of his passage and his mediation; in later tradition it is the instrument that can put the dead to sleep or wake them, the guide of souls between the worlds. [S3] It is the emblem of the messenger, the trader, and the guide. (Note: the caduceus is also later adopted as a medical symbol, but that is a much later, separate use.)
interesting_facts: The caduceus is the Greek equivalent of the "guide of souls" staff; the medical use is a much later, separate adoption.
uncertainty_notes: Whether the two serpents are real or symbolic is debated; the "sleep/wake" property is in the Odyssey but is not a consistent feature in all accounts.
